key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the prosecutrix had left her home voluntarily, of her own free will to get married to the appellant, and that she was 19 years of age and capable of understanding the complications and issues surrounding her marriage to the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, noting contradictions, improvements, and embellishments in their statements, and found that the prosecutrix had not raised any grievance before any person at any stage, suggesting she had submitted to the will of the appellant possibly in lieu of his promise to marry her.
bail_history: The appellant is on bail. His bail bonds stand discharged.

appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeal allowed; conviction and sentences set aside

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant enticed the 19-year-old prosecutrix, wrongfully confined her, and had sexual intercourse with her in lieu of his promise to marry her, leading to conviction under Sections 365 and 376 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecutrix voluntarily left her home to get married to the appellant, had consensual relations with him, and there was no false promise of marriage, thus challenging the conviction.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that consent must be examined for its validity, distinguishing between rape and consensual sex, and emphasized the need to determine if the accused had mala fide intentions.
precedent_relied_upon: Uday v. State of Karnataka AIR 2003 SC 1639; Deelip Singh @ Dilip Kumar v. State of Bihar AIR 2005 SC 203; Yedla Srinivasa Rao v. State of A.P. (2006) 11 SCC 615; Pradeep Kumar Verma v. State of Bihar & Anr. AIR 2007 SC 3059; N. Jaladu, Re /LR (1913) 36 Mad 453
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the conviction under Sections 365 and 376 IPC, but the court set aside the conviction and sentences due to the lack of evidence of a false promise of marriage.
judicial_mitigating_factors: The court considered that the prosecutrix voluntarily left her home to get married to the appellant, was 19 years old, and had consensual relations with him.
